title: Damaged clothing, shoes, or accessories
guidance: Keep the affected items out of picking. If handling is safe, follow the site's damage-hold procedure. Do not return them to sellable stock.
worker_safety: If handling left hands dirty, wash with soap and running water for at least 20 seconds before eating or touching the face. If there is a cut, rash, or unknown contamination, stop handling and get first-aid advice; ordinary handwashing is not treatment for chemical exposure.
report_to: Quality team or floor supervisor, as a damaged-stock report.
clarification: "What damage can you see?" Then clarify the product variant, location, and quantity if known.
escalation: If there is contamination, liquid, sharp material, or an unstable load, stop handling it and involve the safety team.

title: Missing stock or wrong stock count
trigger_examples: fewer hoodies than the recorded count
guidance: Check the exact variant and recorded location. Log the difference between the stored count and what the worker observed; do not automatically change inventory.
report_to: Inventory-control team, as a stock discrepancy.
clarification: "Which product and bin are you checking?" Then ask how many are present, if known.
escalation: If the stock cannot be found or the location is unsafe to access, involve the supervisor. Do not ask the worker to climb or enter a restricted area.

title: Damaged or leaking perfume stock
guidance: Pause handling. If liquid or broken bottles are present, move clear and do not touch or clean the spill. Trained responders use the product safety data sheet and site spill procedure.
worker_safety: If perfume contacted skin, start rinsing with running water immediately for at least 15 minutes and get first-aid/poison-center advice. If splashed in the eyes, rinse immediately for 15–20 minutes; do not rub. Offer the verified wash/eyewash location without delaying rinsing. Serious symptoms require emergency help.
report_to: Safety/spill-response team for a leak; quality team for packaging-only damage.
clarification: From safety: "Is there leaking liquid or broken glass?" Then clarify the location and product if already known.
escalation: Injury, breathing trouble, smoke, or suspected gas requires the site's emergency route; do not wait to finish the report.

title: Broken glass on the floor
trigger_examples: broken fragrance bottle on the floor
guidance: Keep clear of the glass and warn nearby workers from a safe position. Do not pick it up by hand or walk through it. Leave cleanup to trained, authorized staff.
worker_safety: If cut, get a first-aider. For bleeding without embedded glass, apply firm pressure with a clean dressing. Do not remove embedded glass or press directly on it; apply pressure around it. Heavy or uncontrolled bleeding requires emergency help; do not walk off to search for a medical box.
report_to: Safety team, as a broken-glass hazard; first-aid team if someone is injured.
clarification: "Is anyone hurt?" Then ask where the glass is. If liquid is also present, use the spill guidance.
escalation: Serious injury or immediate danger requires emergency help. No photo or SKU is needed before getting help.

title: Damaged boxes, pallets, or leaning stock
guidance: Pause the affected pick or move. Keep clear of an unstable load. Do not pull out supporting boxes, steady the load by hand, or climb the stack.
worker_safety: Wash dirty hands after handling packaging. For splinters, cuts, or a crush injury, stop handling and get a first-aider. Do not dig out embedded objects. Offer a verified first-aid-kit location for minor injuries; serious injury takes the emergency route.
report_to: Floor supervisor or material-handling team; safety team for unstable loads or rack damage.
clarification: "Where is the damaged box or load?" Then clarify what damage was already observed.
escalation: If it may fall or someone is injured, use the site's emergency route. Authorized staff decide when handling can resume.

title: Odd or unknown smell
guidance: Move away from the affected area and report from a safe place. Do not follow the smell, sniff containers, or assume perfume explains it.
worker_safety: If fumes cause irritation or dizziness, move to safe fresh air and get first-aid help. Do not enter the affected area to assist someone; trained responders must handle unsafe rescue. Breathing difficulty or collapse requires emergency help.
report_to: Safety team, as an unknown-odor report.
clarification: Once safe: "Is anyone feeling unwell?" Then ask where the smell was noticed.
escalation: Burning/smoke cues use SOP-09. Suspected gas uses SOP-10. Serious symptoms require emergency help. An unknown source is enough to ask for assistance.

title: Temperature, cooling, or ventilation issue
guidance: Report the affected area to maintenance. If conditions feel unsafe or someone feels unwell, pause work and move to a safe area with suitable conditions. Do not open electrical panels or override equipment.
worker_safety: Offer the first-aider and a verified safe rest area when someone feels unwell. A medical box does not replace medical help for heat/cold illness. Severe symptoms take priority over location lookup or reporting.
report_to: Maintenance and floor supervisor; first-aid team for symptoms.
clarification: "Is anyone feeling unwell?" Then ask which area is affected.
escalation: Confusion, collapse, seizure, or breathing difficulty requires emergency medical help. For suspected heat illness, move to a safe cooler area and start cooling while help is arranged; do not give an unconscious person anything to drink.

escalation: Injury or immediate danger requires emergency help. Authorized dock staff must clear the dock before work resumes.

title: Perfume on skin or in eyes
guidance: For skin contact, immediately remove contaminated clothing and rinse exposed skin with plenty of running water for at least 15 minutes. Mild soap can help remove residue. For an eye splash, immediately rinse with room-temperature water for 15–20 minutes; remove contact lenses if possible without delaying rinsing. Do not rub eyes, use sanitizer on exposed skin, or try to neutralize the substance.
clarification: After rinsing has started: "Was it your skin or your eyes?" Skip if already known. Identify the product only when safe; follow its verified safety data sheet and professional advice.
escalation: Contact a first-aider and the configured poison-advice service. Severe pain or vision changes need urgent medical care; breathing difficulty, collapse, or seizure requires emergency help. Do not wait for symptoms before rinsing.

title: Cut or bleeding after handling stock
trigger_examples: Cut by a bottle, damaged packaging, or sharp product part
guidance: Stop handling and get a first-aider. If nothing is embedded, apply firm direct pressure using a clean dressing. If glass or another object is embedded, leave it in place and apply pressure around it, not onto it. Wear protective gloves when helping another person if available.
clarification: "Is bleeding heavy or not stopping?" Then clarify whether anything is embedded, if not already reported.
escalation: Heavy, continuous, spurting, or uncontrolled bleeding requires emergency help immediately. Ask someone else to bring supplies; do not delay pressure while searching for a kit. Do not prescribe medication or improvised treatment.

title: Find a medical box, first-aider, or wash station
trigger_examples: worker needs a wash station, eyewash, or first-aider following damage or exposure.
guidance: Use verified site records to return the resource name, exact location, and a useful landmark. Give a nearest location only when the worker's location and site layout support that claim. Never invent a location from a product's storage bin.
clarification: "Which area are you in?" Only ask when moving or chatting is safe. If the location is already known, use it.
escalation: If no verified location is available, say so and direct the worker to the floor supervisor or first-aider. Immediate rinsing, bleeding control, and emergency help must not wait for lookup. An injured worker may need someone to bring the kit.
required_site_data: Resource type, name, location/landmark, first-aider contact, and verification date. Actual locations are not yet supplied for this PoC.

title: Report an issue for a coworker
trigger_examples: reporting damage or exposure on someone else's behalf.
guidance: Check that you can stay safely nearby. For collapse, abnormal or absent breathing, severe breathing difficulty, or heavy bleeding, get emergency help immediately. Do not enter a hazardous area to rescue someone. Notify a first-aider and follow the emergency dispatcher's instructions.
clarification: "Are they responsive and breathing normally?" Ask only from safety, without delaying an emergency call. For routine incidents, ask what happened and where; the person's name is optional.
report_to: First-aid/safety team for injury or exposure; quality or inventory team for product-only issues. Record that the worker is reporting on behalf of someone else, and distinguish observed facts from information heard from others.
escalation: Ask a specific nearby person to call emergency services or bring a first-aider while you remain with the affected worker if safe. Do not move someone with a serious injury unless remaining there presents immediate danger. Follow dispatcher guidance for first aid or CPR; do not invent medical instructions.

title: Call 911 or the site's emergency number
trigger_examples: serious injury, collapse, breathing difficulty, fire, or suspected gas leak.
guidance: From a safe location, dial 911 on a phone capable of making calls where 911 is the local emergency number. Elsewhere, use the verified local emergency number. Do not wait to complete a report or obtain supervisor approval. In a suspected gas area, leave before using a phone or this device.
call_script: "We need [medical/fire] help at [verified street address]. The incident is in [warehouse area/dock]. [Describe what happened and the person's condition]. My callback number is [number]." Say what you know; missing details must not delay the call. Follow the dispatcher's questions and instructions, and stay on the line until told to hang up.
escalation: If the Zebra device cannot make a voice call or a call fails, use another available phone from safety and activate the site's emergency reporting method. Never claim the assistant called or reached responders without confirmation. Internal notification does not replace an emergency call.

title: Find an exit or evacuation assembly point
guidance: Follow the site's evacuation instructions and marked exit routes away from danger. In a fire, do not use ordinary elevators. Go to the designated assembly point and report to the person taking attendance. Do not return for stock, belongings, or a medical box.
location_lookup: Use the verified site exit map and the worker's known area. Show the exit name, approved route, and assembly point only when recorded. A map cannot confirm that a route is currently clear; account for reported smoke, gas, or obstructions. Never invent directions or call an exit the nearest without supporting site layout data.
clarification: If safe and the area is unknown: "Which area are you in?" Do not keep a worker chatting instead of leaving. If no verified route is available, tell them to follow marked exits and the site evacuation warden's instructions.
escalation: For a blocked route, use another designated route away from danger. If trapped or unable to evacuate, contact emergency services from safety and give your location; do not cross smoke or a hazardous area. For workers needing assistance, follow the site's assisted-evacuation plan and alert the designated warden; do not improvise a hazardous rescue.
required_site_data: Approved exit routes, alternate routes, assembly points, evacuation-warden contacts, and assisted-evacuation arrangements. Actual exit locations have not yet been supplied.

title: Replenishment request and stock readiness
trigger_examples: What should I check before new stock is received?
guidance: Confirm the exact product, variant, and additional quantity before submitting the request. A destination is not required. When replacement stock arrives, authorized staff check that the product, variant, quantity, and packaging match the request, complete the demo stock-onboarding and registration checks, and record the receipt before stock is made available. Creating a request does not change inventory.
worker_safety: If new stock is leaking, damaged, or unstable, pause handling and use the matching damage or hazard procedure. A restock request alone does not establish that a hazard is present.
report_to: Inventory-control or replenishment team, as a replenishment request after worker confirmation. This is a demo role, not a configured delivery channel.
clarification: Ask only for missing product, variant, or positive additional quantity, one question at a time. Do not ask for a destination. Do not repeat fields already established.
escalation: For a variant absent from the catalog, clarify or offer verified catalog alternatives without substituting stock silently. For an observed hazard, give protective guidance before continuing the request.
demo_rule: Synthetic procedure authored for this proof of concept; not a retailer-approved receiving process. Receiving, stock registration, inventory changes, task assignment, and notifications are not performed merely by showing this guidance.
short_response: When stock arrives, check the product, variant, quantity, and packaging. Authorized staff must complete receiving and stock registration before it becomes available.

title: Worker coughing, feverish, or feeling unwell
trigger_examples: My teammate is coughing a lot
My coworker has a high fever
guidance: Pause the affected work and seek the supervisor or first-aider for help. For cough or fever that may be a respiratory illness, avoid close contact with others and follow the site illness-reporting process. Record only the reported symptoms or observations; do not diagnose a cold, flu, or infection or prescribe medication.
worker_safety: Trouble breathing or chest pain requires emergency medical help immediately. If coughing started near fumes, a spill, or an unusual smell, also use the matching exposure or unknown-odor procedure; do not assume infection explains it.
report_to: Floor supervisor or first-aid team, as a general-concern report. The person reporting may be a coworker; personal names are not needed for the synthetic demo.

Worker coughing, feverish, or feeling unwell
Situations: My teammate is coughing a lot; A worker has a cold; My coworker has a high fever; I feel feverish; Someone is feeling unwell
Guidance: Pause the affected work and seek the supervisor or first-aider for help. For cough or fever that may be a respiratory illness, avoid close contact with others and follow the site illness-reporting process. Record only the reported symptoms or observations; do not diagnose a cold, flu, or infection or prescribe medication.
Worker safety: Trouble breathing or chest pain requires emergency medical help immediately. If coughing started near fumes, a spill, or an unusual smell, also use the matching exposure or unknown-odor procedure; do not assume infection explains it.
